# libdiginet / fuzz_frame

libdiginet's own fuzz target `fuzz_frame` ([source](source/fuzz_frame.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libdiginet 0.1.1 (FreeMixer/libdiginet at 835f336c).

Treats the input as one Ethernet frame (checksum excluded), copied into an allocation of its exact length. It parses the frame with the library and with its own reader written from the protocol grammar, then compares the refusal codes and every header field, rebuilds the frame from the parsed fields and compares it byte for byte with the grammar's frame, and checks the announce reader on announce frames. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libdiginet at commit 835f336c: the frame, command cursor, controls and decoder sources and the session state machine, built into one static library. The packet socket and descriptor io are not built; the library's own libFuzzer build uses the same sources.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The parser refuses exactly the frames the protocol grammar refuses (too short, wrong EtherType, a length field under 16 or past the buffer), each with its documented error code ([lines 34-63](source/fuzz_frame.c#L34-L63)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- For an accepted frame, every header field, both MAC addresses, the EtherType, the body and its padding, the 16-bit body sum and whether the header carries it, the Digidesign OUI test of the source address and the keepalive test are what the protocol grammar reads at the same offsets ([lines 65-112](source/fuzz_frame.c#L65-L112)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- From the fields the grammar reads, the frame builder makes, in both sum modes, exactly the frame the harness builds itself from the protocol (sum or zero, padding to 60 bytes included); it refuses a body past 1484 bytes, a body holding the system family and a buffer one byte short, and writes nothing into a refused buffer ([lines 114-200](source/fuzz_frame.c#L114-L200)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The announce reader accepts only an e0 or e1 frame of at least 33 body bytes and reads the unknown bytes, the version and the name at their documented offsets, each cut and terminated as documented ([lines 212-263](source/fuzz_frame.c#L212-L263)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libdiginet` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |

| plain | `fuzz_frame.plain` | 47,664 | `18df03196c1357ef24f1fda83c7378a98d136a1ae0df11fe3b00db00e52d272e` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
